scenes.label: Meet the team
scenes.title: The Connection Lab
scenes.caption: Neel builds a tiny paper-strip sorter in the Connection Lab. Its visible rule predicts the label of the nearest selected length. This is a classroom model with invented numbers, not a claim that every AI system learns in exactly this way.

scenes.label: The problem
scenes.title: What changed?
scenes.caption: At first, Neel selects only a short-strip example. The model then predicts short even for a much longer strip. Tara adds checked examples from both categories and compares predictions again. More copies of the first example would not supply the missing coverage of longer strips.

scenes.label: How it works
scenes.title: Follow the evidence
scenes.caption: The check cards are separate from the selectable training cards. The team records both correct predictions and mistakes, then tries a changed set. Passing these few invented checks supports a narrow classroom result; unfamiliar lengths and different tasks still need review before any wider use.

scenes.label: Your decision
scenes.title: Decide and explain
scenes.caption: Long check strips are being predicted as short because the selected training set contains no long example. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.speech: Long check strips are being predicted as short because the selected training set contains no long example. Compare the actions, then explain which evidence supports your decision.
scenes.dialogue: Only short examples were selected. What should change?

scenes.label: What changes
scenes.title: Check the consequence
scenes.caption: Add checked long examples and rerun the check. This supplies relevant coverage, while copying short examples would leave the same gap.

scenes.title: Investigate in the lab
scenes.caption: Investigate nearest-number predictions, then training coverage, then changed examples. Test your plan, read feedback and try a changed case. Save evidence; explain one limitation.
